name: Recursion
summary: Foundational technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with smaller sub-problems until a trivial case is reached.

name: Base Case
summary: The terminating condition that yields a direct result without further recursive calls, preventing unbounded recursion.

name: Recursive Case
summary: The execution path where the problem is reduced and the function invokes itself on smaller inputs to build toward the final solution.

name: Termination
summary: The formal guarantee that every recursive call makes monotonic progress toward a base case, preventing call stack overflow.
